priority_legend.P1: Core workflows, coordination and existing model routing

summary: Fifteen engineering outcomes: preserve the approved trading fixes, make regression lessons reusable across all skills, verify database-backed backtesting and paper history, record evidence, and deliver one improvement skill in JarvisDaily chat. Coordination and superseded items remain in appendices.

requirements.title: Complete every required protective exit
requirements.problem: A reported stop-loss closed only part of a position, leaving the rest for manual intervention.
requirements.requested_outcome: Complete and confirm the intended protective exit for the affected strategy’s full remaining quantity, without closing another strategy’s position.
requirements.observed_incident: Reported incomplete protective exit; the cause is not verified.
hypothesized_causes: Shared handling, delayed updates and deployment changes were discussed as possible explanations.

evidence.summary: The caller reported that half the intended quantity had not exited.
The caller emphasized that missed stop-loss execution was unacceptable.

acceptance_checks.text: Check that the reported partial-exit case closes the full intended quantity in a controlled test.
Test partial fills, delayed updates and an interrupted exit, including how the remaining quantity is identified and handled.
Distinguish an exit request, a partial fill and a confirmed full exit.

requirements.title: Prevent one strategy from blocking another valid entry
requirements.problem: Similar strategies operating together were reported to miss valid entries, including on previously working accounts.
requirements.requested_outcome: Process each eligible strategy entry independently and explain any valid rejection or delay.
requirements.observed_incident: Reported missed entries when similar strategies operated together.
hypothesized_causes: The other strategy’s quantity or a delayed update may have affected a safety check.

evidence.summary: The speakers described missed entries when similar strategies ran together and committed to correcting the platform behaviour.

acceptance_checks.text: Test simultaneous entries for two strategies on the same instrument and account, with either strategy confirmed first.
Confirm both eligible entries complete once each; retain real safety checks and clear reasons for rejection.
Repeat across more than one affected configuration.

requirements.title: Keep even identical strategies independent
requirements.problem: Strategies that share an account and instrument must not interfere with one another.
requirements.requested_outcome: Keep each strategy independent even when its entry rules, exits, stops, quantity and account are identical to another strategy.

evidence.summary: The client asked for completely identical strategies to behave independently.
The client said one strategy’s stop-loss must not exit another strategy.

acceptance_checks.text: Test two identical strategies together and track their entries, quantities, protection and exits separately.
An exit in one strategy must not close or remove protection from the other.
Repeat with different stop-loss and exit rules and newly added similar strategies.

requirements.decision_needed: Approve independent behaviour; choose the technical design after investigating.

requirements.title: Send each strategy the updates it needs
requirements.problem: A speaker suggested that one strategy may receive an update that another also needs, leaving the second unable to act.
requirements.requested_outcome: Deliver relevant updates to every intended strategy, with each acting only on its own position and instructions.
hypothesized_causes: One strategy consuming an update needed by another was suggested but not proven.
proposed_approaches: The call suggested distributing relevant updates to both strategies for independent assessment.

evidence.summary: The conversation proposed giving both strategy versions the relevant incoming update for independent assessment.
The client asked that each strategy check whether an update belongs to it.

acceptance_checks.text: Show that each intended strategy receives the relevant update and identifies its own action.
Test delayed, repeated and out-of-order updates without missed actions or duplicate orders.
Distributing an update to several strategies must not create extra broker orders.

requirements.decision_needed: Validate the cause before choosing an update-routing design.

requirements.title: Match shared broker positions to the correct strategies
requirements.problem: The broker may show a combined position while the platform needs to know each strategy’s share.
requirements.requested_outcome: Keep each strategy’s quantity accurate when several strategies share an account and instrument, while preserving safety checks.
hypothesized_causes: Combined broker quantity and shared processing were discussed as possible sources of interference.
proposed_approaches: Keep an accurate platform record of each strategy’s actions and quantity.

evidence.summary: The speakers noted that the broker does not label a combined position by strategy version and discussed distinguishing the strategies within the platform.

acceptance_checks.text: Match the combined broker quantity to the quantities assigned to the relevant strategies during entries, partial fills and exits.
Test a manual exit without assigning its effect to an unrelated strategy.
Keep any unexplained difference visible instead of assuming that all positions are closed or bypassing a safety check.

requirements.title: Test all important similar-strategy combinations
requirements.problem: The client asked for a broader review instead of repeatedly repairing only the latest symptom.
requirements.requested_outcome: Test the meaningful combinations of similar strategies before declaring the reliability work complete.

evidence.summary: The client requested a broad review of similar-strategy combinations and additional possible failures.
The developer described the intended result as reliable operation for newly added similar strategies too.

acceptance_checks.text: Cover identical and different rules, simultaneous and staggered entries, both update orders, partial exits, manual exits and multiple accounts.
Add a repeatable check for every reproduced incident, including missed entries and incomplete exits.
Check correctness and response time under realistic delays; efficiency must not hide failures.

requirements.title: Review how each change affects existing features
requirements.problem: The client wants likely interactions considered before a change creates another operational problem.
requirements.requested_outcome: Before implementation, identify how the change could affect existing behaviour and how existing behaviour could affect the new change.

evidence.summary: The client asked for a two-way impact review between a new change and previously implemented behaviour.

acceptance_checks.text: Record the affected workflows and likely interaction problems.
Check previous supported behaviour as well as the new feature’s expected result.

requirements.title: Make regression lessons a mandatory shared check
requirements.problem: The existing tests and operational skills need to carry forward incident lessons so the same failures are caught before completion or release is claimed.
requirements.requested_outcome: Extend the existing integration suite and use one shared verification gate from every repository skill. Cover past incidents, current supported strategies and newly added strategies, then produce an evidence-based readiness result for the exact code and data tested.

evidence.summary: The call described an earlier testing cycle leaving issues unresolved.
The speakers emphasized completing integration testing and preserving existing behaviour.
The client allowed delaying a change by a day if more review or testing was needed.

The feedback requests reuse of the existing integration suite and a runnable verification skill that captures every lesson. The revised item also retains the technical readiness and exposure checks from the coordination items.

acceptance_checks.text: Maintain an incident and regression registry linking each known failure to its expected behaviour, a repeatable test, affected strategy features and proof of the result. Include the approved independence, missed-entry, partial-exit and manual-exit cases.

Cover legacy supported versions, current configurations and new strategy features in a maintained test matrix. New strategies or changed features must select the relevant existing checks and add any missing regression case.

Reuse the existing integration suite through a shared gate. Inventory every repository skill and connect it to that gate with its applicable checks, including the existing health-check and verification workflows. Keep shared rules in one place.

Record the exact code commit, strategy/configuration revisions, data revision or reproducible data fingerprint, environment, selected checks and results. A relevant code or data change makes older evidence insufficient.

Missing required tests, missing data, unfinished checks or failures produce a clear not-verified result. Service tests, review-page tests or skill-file checks do not by themselves prove trading behaviour.

Keep a release or restart blocked when required checks fail or are unfinished. Before disruptive work or a trading restart, reconcile actual open positions and pending orders; a paused strategy or a successful process restart is not proof that exposure is safe.

Demonstrate the gate detecting a known failure and passing the repaired case in a controlled environment. Give the responsible operator a readiness report with remaining blockers rather than a guarantee that no future defect can occur.

Assign each incident action an owner, expected closure evidence and tracking reference. Track recurrence, unresolved discrepancies and verification coverage over stated observation periods; a merged change alone does not close the action.

retained_scope_notes: Client scheduling and maintenance-window coordination remain in the appendix; technical release and restart checks remain here.

requirements.title: Compare backtests with three to four months of linked trade history
requirements.problem: The client needs more than a matching summary from a few trades; paper and actual trading records must be traceable to the comparable backtest.
requirements.requested_outcome: Use the available three-to-four-month history for supported strategies to compare backtest, paper and live results at trade level. Link each expected entry and exit, explain differences and correct defects without hiding data gaps.
requirements.observed_incident: The call contained conflicting claims about matching results. The shared database-backed comparison remains the evidence needed to resolve them.

evidence.summary: The client reported older-period backtest results that did not match.
Another speaker said the July, August and September comparisons already matched.
The feedback specifies existing three-to-four-month history and linked entry/exit comparison against paper or actual trading. The larger-sample request is included here.

acceptance_checks.text: Build a coverage report for every supported strategy and relevant version, targeting three to four months where stored history exists. Include longer samples and multiple strategies; if coverage is shorter, show the exact gap and limit the conclusion.

Lock the strategy version, parameters, period, timezone, market-data revision and execution/cost assumptions before comparison. Use the same baseline for paper, live and backtest comparisons where the records are comparable.
Link entries, exits and partial fills to the corresponding strategy and expected trade. Compare counts, directions, quantities, times, prices and outcomes, and list unmatched or duplicated records.
Separate missing data, retrieval problems, strategy-engine differences and real execution differences such as fills, timing or costs. Define any comparison tolerance before running the check.

Provide a repeatable comparison report with evidence for each unexplained difference. Fix defects and rerun affected cases; label unresolved or unavailable coverage not verified rather than forcing totals to match.
Use time-correct market inputs and strategy versions. Stored paper and live trades are comparison evidence, never future-known answers supplied to a backtest; test explicitly for look-ahead leakage.

requirements.title: Use the complete available database history reliably
requirements.problem: History selection failed, and the feedback raised a concern that backtesting and AI may not be retrieving the stored paper-trade history they need. The cause still needs verification.
requirements.requested_outcome: Make stored strategy, paper-trade and live-trade records the traceable basis for backtesting and JarvisDaily analysis. Retrieve the complete available history relevant to the selected strategy and period, and keep the account/strategy filters and historical results usable.
requirements.observed_incident: History selection and result visibility failures were reported. Whether records were missing or merely not retrieved is unverified.
hypothesized_causes: Incomplete data retrieval was suggested in review feedback. It remains a hypothesis until storage and query evidence are checked.

evidence.summary: During the call, the user could not select an account or strategy.
The user reported being unable to see a previous paper-trade result.
The feedback emphasizes the value of the existing database and asks that the engine and AI use the full relevant history, while preserving the original history-usability requirement.

acceptance_checks.text: Inventory the relevant stored records and their coverage by strategy version, account scope, date and execution mode. Check for missing intervals, stale results, incomplete retrieval, duplicates and broken links between entries and exits.
Retrieve all relevant available records for the chosen scope, including pagination or long histories. Show which records and data revision each backtest or AI analysis used.
Keep paper, live and backtest records distinct and enforce the user’s permitted account scope. Missing or incomplete data must be shown explicitly rather than invented or treated as a zero outcome.
Verify account and strategy selection, open a known historical result, and repeat after a refresh or update. Distinguish no matching records from a loading failure or maintenance.

Trace a detected data gap from storage through retrieval to the result, fix its actual cause and rerun the affected analysis. Do not assume that missing data explains every failure or that complete data guarantees correct logic.

Keep recorded outcomes separate from the market inputs available at each historical decision time. Data retrieval must preserve timestamps and versions and must not leak future trade outcomes into simulation or AI evaluation.

requirements.title: Record video evidence and close the observed gaps
requirements.problem: The approved report-sharing item received additional feedback asking for recordings across the supported strategy workflows and investigation of any gaps.
requirements.requested_outcome: Produce accessible comparison reports and a recorded walkthrough covering the supported strategies being verified, including JarvisDaily’s use of strategy/history data. Show gaps, diagnose their causes, fix defects and record the affected checks again.

evidence.summary: The client requested a message identifying the exact report to inspect.
The review adds video evidence across the strategies being tested and asks that observed data or workflow gaps be diagnosed, corrected and recorded.

acceptance_checks.text: Use a video coverage index to identify each supported strategy or feature configuration, report/run, code revision and data revision demonstrated. Include failed or unavailable cases rather than showing only a successful example.

Record selection of the strategy and data, the backtest or paper workflow, linked entry/exit results and the relevant comparison. Demonstrate the JarvisDaily skill using the same traceable data, including the one-strategy pilot.

For each gap, distinguish missing records, failed retrieval, configuration problems and engine or AI behaviour. Record the evidence, correction and rerun; a lack of data is a possible cause, not an assumed explanation for every failure.
Keep a clear report link or identifier and ensure the intended reviewer can open the video and supporting evidence. Protect private account details in shared recordings.
Summarize verified coverage and remaining not-verified cases. The earlier approval of report sharing remains historical; this expanded video requirement needs a fresh review.

requirements.revision_note: Expanded from the previously approved report-sharing wording to include video coverage and gap diagnosis. Requires fresh review.

requirements.title: Run every supported strategy through backtesting and paper trading
requirements.problem: The user needs a dependable workflow for developing strategies, with clear results and clear explanations when data or features are unavailable.
requirements.requested_outcome: Make the supported strategy set runnable in backtesting and paper trading using the verified stored history, and show complete, understandable results and data limitations.

evidence.summary: The client asked to be able to backtest any supported strategy that evening; the response included paper trading.
The original request for usable backtesting and paper trading is retained. The deadline is moved out of engineering scope, while coverage and data-backed results are made measurable.

acceptance_checks.text: Use the maintained supported-strategy and feature matrix to run each supported configuration through backtesting and the relevant paper-trading workflow.
Open the completed result and its linked trade history, confirm the data/configuration used, and make missing data or unsupported settings visible.
Record failures with their actual causes, correct them and rerun affected cases. Make no supported case disappear silently or count an unverified case as passed.
Capture the successful and unresolved cases in the reports and video evidence, and run the shared regression gate for the resulting code and data revision.

requirements.title: Build one reusable improvement skill in JarvisDaily chat
requirements.problem: The repeated AI requests describe one workflow: use an existing strategy and its data to research better exits, preserve winning outcomes where possible and reduce losses without requiring a new screen.
requirements.requested_outcome: Create one reusable strategy-improvement skill accessible through the existing JarvisDaily chat. Use the selected strategy and full relevant stored history, keep entries fixed by default, test allowed exit changes and return a reproducible comparison. Deliver a one-strategy pilot and then reuse the same workflow across supported strategies.

evidence.summary: The developer offered a reusable skill and ready-made prompt.
The feedback explicitly consolidates this work into one skill accessible through JarvisDaily chat, repeats the profit/loss improvement goal and identifies the other AI items as the same requirement.

acceptance_checks.text: Expose the skill through the existing JarvisDaily chat with a ready-made prompt and plain instructions. The user selects an existing strategy and analysis scope in that flow; no separate tab, module or new application is part of this scope.
Retrieve the strategy definition and complete relevant database history, show its coverage and record the exact code/configuration/data revisions. Explain missing input before drawing a conclusion.

Keep the entry rules and baseline entry set identical in every candidate by default. Explore only approved indicators, exit conditions, stops, trailing stops and targets; do not delete entries to improve a result.

On the fixed dataset, evaluate the aspiration to preserve at least 80% of baseline winning outcomes while tolerating changes to up to 20%, and to reduce losses across all baseline losing trades. Report feasibility and trade-offs; these are measured research aims, not guaranteed results.

Report unchanged winners and winners that remain profitable separately. For every baseline losing trade, report whether loss improved, stayed the same or worsened; distinguish evaluating all losers from actually improving all of them.

Compare baseline and candidate net profit/loss, return or ROI, win rate, risk/reward and linked trade outcomes using the same data, entry set and declared cost assumptions. Publish the metric definitions and classify break-even or unavailable outcomes separately.
Show each attempted change, rationale and result, including no improvement or a worse result. Test a separate period where sufficient data exists and disclose its coverage.

Demonstrate the complete workflow on one existing strategy, record pilot feedback and verify another supported strategy can run without rewriting the skill. Keep experiments bounded, report progress and measure elapsed time and manual effort saved.

Keep generated strategy changes as reviewable research drafts. Backtest or paper results do not change live strategies or authorize orders. Include the new behaviour and data-gap cases in the shared regression gate.
Use only information available at each simulated decision time. Trade outcomes may label the comparison after the run but must not supply future-known answers to the strategy.

Report cost-adjusted net return and maximum drawdown as well as the other metrics. Choose the holdout period before tuning, log every attempt including losing candidates, and do not claim that one improved backtest proves the strategy avoids overfitting.

Keep the fixed-entry experiment distinct from an independently rerun candidate. If changed exits affect eligibility for later entries, report that difference and its effect separately rather than hiding it or silently changing the baseline entry set.

scope_decisions: Use one skill in existing JarvisDaily chat; do not create a new tab or module.
Keep entries fixed by default. The illustrative smaller entry count does not authorize entry removal.
Treat improvement percentages and turnaround expectations as measurable aspirations, not guaranteed profit or a fixed delivery-time promise.
The example of 1:2 risk/reward and a win rate above 50% is not a mandatory acceptance target.
requirements.metric_definition_policy: Before each experiment, record the baseline classification and exact formulas. Show unchanged and still-profitable winners separately, and show losing-trade coverage and actual improvement separately. Use locked precision and cost assumptions so apparent improvement is not a changed sample or calculation.

quality_mechanism.title: Proposed evidence and reliability checks
quality_mechanism.summary: These proposed checks translate the linked sources into an engineering verification approach. They do not establish that the gate is implemented or that current live strategies have passed it.
quality_mechanism.classification: Adapted engineering proposals, not publisher guarantees or an audit of the live platform.

practices.outcome: A reported failure becomes a reproducible, versioned verification case.
practices.acceptance: The evidence bundle records available input coverage, state, versions and expected behaviour. Missing evidence is explicitly tracked; an unreproducible incident is not described as proven fixed.

practices.outcome: Ownership and lifecycle are verified through failures and restarts.
practices.acceptance: A required fault-injection suite covers partial fills, close/reduce/protective exits, timeout-after-acceptance, concurrent retry, restart and multiple strategies on one symbol. Known unresolved exposure remains visible.

practices.outcome: Paper and live differences are measured using comparable evidence.
practices.acceptance: Report input/state/configuration differences, decision differences and execution differences separately. Freshness limits and numerical tolerances are documented before the run; missing-data periods cannot silently count as successful coverage.

practices.outcome: Promotion depends on required evidence, with a defined recovery procedure.
practices.acceptance: Publish the tested artifact hashes, scenario coverage, stage metrics, gate results and owner. Unmet gates prevent promotion. Recovery rehearsals preserve and reconcile existing exposure.

practices.outcome: Reliability progress is visible independently of model confidence.
practices.acceptance: Review recurrence, unexplained decision mismatches, unresolved order/exposure age, detection/recovery time, failed releases and overdue preventive actions. Record denominators and observation windows rather than presenting isolated success counts.

sources.title: Live Trading: Reconciliation
supported_claims: QuantConnect compares live deployments with parallel out-of-sample backtests to measure divergence.
Arrival timing, corrected historical data, fill models, initial holdings and lost restart state can change results.
caveats: These replay checks are an AlgoVeda proposal, not a QuantConnect guarantee. Identical historical candles alone do not prove identical inputs. Exact live fills cannot be guaranteed by simulation.

sources.title: Kite Connect 3: Orders
supported_claims: An accepted placement and returned order_id do not establish exchange receipt or execution. Order details/history establish actual status.
The order book is retained for the current day. A tag identifies an order but is not documented as a broker deduplication guarantee.
caveats: The ownership ledger is our design inference. Account net positions alone do not establish strategy ownership. Local idempotency does not make an uncertain broker submission safe to repeat.

sources.title: Kite Connect 3: Postbacks / WebHooks
supported_claims: UPDATE notifications include partial fills. Payloads provide user/order identity and filled, pending and cancelled quantities.
App webhooks cover orders placed through that API key; user WebSocket updates cover orders placed through other user interfaces. Webhook checksums should be validated.
caveats: The documentation does not promise exactly-once or ordered notification delivery. Duplicate/reordering tests are defensive proposals. Order reconciliation is separate from the live market-data stream.

sources.title: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
supported_claims: Caller-provided request identifiers express intent; recording the token and related service mutations must be atomic.
A reused identifier with changed parameters should be rejected. Retention must account for late requests and resource lifetime.
caveats: AWS describes contracts implemented by AWS services. Kite does not inherit those contracts; a local transaction cannot atomically commit a remote broker order. Uncertainty must be handled explicitly.

sources.title: The Site Reliability Workbook: Canarying Releases
supported_claims: Repeatable builds, automated tests, small releases and measured rollout stages reduce release risk.
Canaries need representative duration, attributable metrics and an adequate control; shared dependencies can contaminate comparisons. Defined limits can stop or roll back a rollout.
caveats: Trading adaptation requires separate paper/live ledgers. Code rollback does not reverse executed trades or automatically make open-position management safe; rehearse that recovery path separately.

sources.title: The Site Reliability Workbook: Postmortem Culture
supported_claims: Effective preventive actions have owners, priorities, tracking identifiers and verifiable end states.
Repeated incidents warrant checking whether actions are overdue, insufficient or displaced by feature work. Follow-up tooling tracks action closure.
caveats: This precise closure chain is our adaptation. No regression corpus covers every future condition; monitor outcomes and revise controls when failures recur.
